  - Debugger panel:
    * "Registers" table: V0..VF as two hex digits each, in a 4x4 grid or 16 rows; highlight VF.

=== EMULATOR CORE (JavaScript) ===
Implement a class `Chip8` with:
- `memory = new Uint8Array(4096)`
- `V = new Uint8Array(16)`
- `I = 0` (16-bit index register)
- `pc = 0x200`
- `stack = new Uint16Array(16)`, `sp = 0`
- `delayTimer = 0`, `soundTimer = 0`
- `gfx = new Uint8Array(64*32)` (1 = pixel on)
- `keys = new Uint8Array(16)` (0/1)
- `waitingForKey = false`, `waitReg = 0`
- `halted = false` (set by 0x00FD EXIT)
- `lastOpcode = 0`, `lastDisasm = ''`
- `hires = false` (not used for display, but keep for 00FE/00FF)

Font set: the standard 16 hex-digit sprites (0-F), 5 bytes each, 80 bytes total, loaded at 0x050. Use the canonical font:
0: F0 90 90 90 F0
1: 20 60 20 20 70
2: F0 10 F0 80 F0
3: F0 10 F0 10 F0
4: 90 90 F0 10 10
5: F0 80 F0 10 F0
6: F0 80 F0 90 F0
7: F0 10 20 40 40
8: F0 90 F0 90 F0
9: F0 90 F0 10 F0
A: F0 90 F0 90 90
B: E0 90 E0 90 E0
C: F0 80 80 80 F0
D: E0 90 90 90 E0
E: F0 80 F0 80 F0
F: F0 80 F0 80 80
Also a big-font set (16 x 10 bytes) at 0x0A0 for Fx30 (SCHIP) — optional but include it.

`reset()`: memory.fill(0); V.fill(0); gfx.fill(0); keys.fill(0); stack.fill(0); sp=0; I=0; pc=0x200; delayTimer=0; soundTimer=0; waitingForKey=false; halted=false; lastOpcode=0; load font at 0x050 (and big font at 0x0A0); then if a ROM is loaded, copy it to 0x200. Reset cycle counter.

`loadROM(bytes)`: reset(), then for i in bytes: memory[0x200+i] = bytes[i] & 0xFF (guard against >3584 bytes).

`cycle()` — fetch/decode/execute exactly one instruction:
```
if (this.halted) return;
if (this.waitingForKey) return;   // stall: PC not advanced until key pressed
const op = (memory[pc] << 8) | memory[pc+1];
this.lastOpcode = op; this.lastDisasm = disassemble(op);
this.pc = (this.pc + 2) & 0xFFF;
... decode ...
```
Note: set lastOpcode/lastDisasm to the instruction being executed, and keep a separate `nextOpcode` accessor for the debugger that reads memory[pc] at display time.

Decode (complete classic 35 + SCHIP extras):
- `0x00E0` CLS: gfx.fill(0)
- `0x00EE` RET: sp--; pc = stack[sp]
- `0x0000` NOP
- `(op & 0xFFF0) === 0x00C0` SCD n: scroll display down n pixels (shift gfx rows)
- `0x00FB` SCR: scroll right 4 px
- `0x00FC` SCL: scroll left 4 px
- `0x00FD` EXIT: halted = true
- `0x00FE` LOW: hires = false
- `0x00FF` HIGH: hires = true
- `0x1NNN` JP addr: pc = NNN
- `0x2NNN` CALL addr: stack[sp++] = pc; pc = NNN
- `0x3XKK` SE Vx, byte: if (V[x] === kk) pc += 2
- `0x4XKK` SNE Vx, byte: if (V[x] !== kk) pc += 2
- `0x5XY0` SE Vx, Vy: if (V[x] === V[y]) pc += 2
- `0x6XKK` LD Vx, byte: V[x] = kk
- `0x7XKK` ADD Vx, byte: V[x] = (V[x] + kk) & 0xFF   (no carry flag)
- `0x8XY0` LD Vx, Vy: V[x] = V[y]
- `0x8XY1` OR: V[x] |= V[y]; (V[0xF] = 0 on SCHIP — do NOT clear, keep classic behavior: leave VF alone)
- `0x8XY2` AND: V[x] &= V[y]
- `0x8XY3` XOR: V[x] ^= V[y]
- `0x8XY4` ADD: const sum = V[x] + V[y]; V[0xF] = sum > 255 ? 1 : 0; V[x] = sum & 0xFF
- `0x8XY5` SUB: const f = V[x] >= V[y] ? 1 : 0; V[x] = (V[x] - V[y]) & 0xFF; V[0xF] = f   (VF = NOT borrow)
- `0x8XY6` SHR: if legacyShift { V[x] = V[y]; } const f = V[x] & 1; V[x] = V[x] >> 1; V[0xF] = f
- `0x8XY7` SUBN: const f = V[y] >= V[x] ? 1 : 0; V[x] = (V[y] - V[x]) & 0xFF; V[0xF] = f
- `0x8XYE` SHL: if legacyShift { V[x] = V[y]; } const f = (V[x] >> 7) & 1; V[x] = (V[x] << 1) & 0xFF; V[0xF] = f
- `0x9XY0` SNE Vx, Vy: if (V[x] !== V[y]) pc += 2
- `0xANNN` LD I, addr: I = NNN
- `0xBNNN` JP V0, addr: pc = (NNN + V[0]) & 0xFFF
- `0xCXKK` RND: V[x] = (Math.random() * 256) & 0xFF & kk  -> use `V[x] = (Math.floor(Math.random()*256) & 0xFF) & kk`
- `0xDXYN` DRW: XOR sprite. 
  ```
  const x0 = V[x] & 63, y0 = V[y] & 31;
  V[0xF] = 0;
  for (let row = 0; row < n; row++) {
    const py = (y0 + row) % 32;
    const bits = memory[(I + row) & 0xFFF];
    for (let col = 0; col < 8; col++) {
      if ((bits & (0x80 >> col)) !== 0) {
        const px = (x0 + col) % 64;
        const idx = py * 64 + px;
        if (gfx[idx]) V[0xF] = 1;
        gfx[idx] ^= 1;
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  IMPORTANT: V[0xF] must be set AFTER the loop or the loop must not clobber it — since we only write gfx and V[0xF], and the sprite reads V[x]/V[y] which may be VF... To be safe, capture `x0`/`y0` BEFORE clearing V[0xF] (done above).
- `0xEX9E` SKP Vx: if (keys[V[x] & 0xF]) pc += 2
- `0xEXA1` SKNP Vx: if (!keys[V[x] & 0xF]) pc += 2
- `0xFX07` LD Vx, DT: V[x] = delayTimer
- `0xFX0A` LD Vx, K: waitingForKey = true; waitReg = x   (do NOT advance further; PC already advanced past this instruction so that when the key arrives we just set V[x] and resume)
- `0xFX15` LD DT, Vx: delayTimer = V[x]
- `0xFX18` LD ST, Vx: soundTimer = V[x]
- `0xFX1E` ADD I, Vx: I = (I + V[x]) & 0xFFF
- `0xFX29` LD F, Vx: I = 0x050 + (V[x] & 0xF) * 5
- `0xFX30` LD HF, Vx: I = 0x0A0 + (V[x] & 0xF) * 10   (big font)
- `0xFX33` BCD: memory[I] = Math.floor(V[x]/100); memory[I+1] = Math.floor(V[x]/10)%10; memory[I+2] = V[x]%10
- `0xFX55` LD [I], Vx: for (let i=0;i<=x;i++) memory[(I+i)&0xFFF] = V[i];  (do NOT modify I)
- `0xFX65` LD Vx, [I]: for (let i=0;i<=x;i++) V[i] = memory[(I+i)&0xFFF]
- `0x5XY2` (SCHIP) LD [I], Vx..Vy: store range
- `0x5XY3` (SCHIP) LD Vx..Vy, [I]: load range
- `0xFX75` LD R, Vx: store V0..Vx into flags array (keep a `flags = new Uint8Array(16)`)
- `0xFX85` LD Vx, R: load flags
- default: unknown opcode -> do nothing but count it (and show it in the debugger as "UNKNOWN").

Also implement `disassemble(op)` returning a human-readable string for every opcode above (e.g. "DRW V0, V1, 8  ; draw 8-byte sprite at (V0,V1), XOR, VF=collision"). Unknown -> "UNKNOWN 0xXXXX".

`tickTimers()`: if (delayTimer > 0) delayTimer--; if (soundTimer > 0) soundTimer--;  — called at exactly 60 Hz.

`pressKey(k)` / `releaseKey(k)`: set keys[k]; if waitingForKey and pressed, V[waitReg] = k, waitingForKey = false.

=== MAIN LOOP / DRIVER ===
- Use `requestAnimationFrame`. Maintain `lastTimerTime`; every >= 1000/60 ms call `chip8.tickTimers()` (use an accumulator so drift is fine).
- If state === 'running': run `ipsPerFrame` instructions (from the slider) each animation frame, but cap total work per frame to avoid freezing (e.g. max 2000).
- Track cycles executed; compute a measured IPS over a 1-second window and display it.
- `render()`: draw gfx to the canvas via ImageData (create ImageData once, set RGBA per pixel: on -> foreground color, off -> black), then ctx.putImageData. Also draw a subtle grid? No — keep it clean, just pixels.
- Sound: create an AudioContext lazily on first user gesture; a single oscillator + gain; when soundTimer > 0 and soundOn checked, start/keep the oscillator at ~440 Hz with low gain; otherwise stop it. Guard against browsers without AudioContext.
- Keyboard handling: `keydown`/`keyup` on window. Map physical keys to CHIP-8 keys using the table: '1'->0x1,'2'->0x2,'3'->0x3,'4'->0xC,'q'->0x4,'w'->0x5,'e'->0x6,'r'->0xD,'a'->0x7,'s'->0x8,'d'->0x9,'f'->0xE,'z'->0xA,'x'->0x0,'c'->0xB,'v'->0xF. - Update the on-screen keypad button highlight classes from `chip8.keys` every frame (so both physical and on-screen presses show).
- Update the debugger panel every frame (or every ~4 frames for perf) with registers, I, PC, SP, stack, timers, current instruction (raw + disasm), last executed instruction, and VF flag.
- Step button: pause, then execute exactly one `cycle()` (and render + update debugger).
- Reset button: `chip8.reset(); chip8.loadROM(currentROM);` re-render, pause.
- Demo ROM button: load the built-in demo ROM and run.
- On load: automatically load and run the built-in demo ROM so the emulator is immediately usable with no download.

=== BUILT-IN DEMO ROM (exact bytes, must be used verbatim) ===
```
const DEMO_ROM = new Uint8Array([
  0x18,0x3C,0x7E,0xFF,0xFF,0x7E,0x3C,0x18,
  0x60,0x00, 0x61,0x00, 0x62,0x02, 0x63,0x02,
  0x65,0x02, 0x66,0x37, 0x67,0x17, 0x6A,0x05,
  0xA2,0x00, 0x00,0xE0,
  0xD0,0x18,
  0x80,0x40, 0x84,0x55, 0x4F,0x00, 0x62,0x02,
  0x80,0x40, 0x84,0x66, 0x4F,0x01, 0x62,0xFE,
  0x80,0x04,
  0x81,0x40, 0x84,0x55, 0x4F,0x00, 0x63,0x02,
  0x81,0x40, 0x84,0x77, 0x4F,0x01, 0x63,0xFE,
  0x81,0x04,
  0xEA,0x9E, 0x12,0x1A,
  0x62,0xFE, 0x63,0xFE, 0x12,0x1A

```
This is a real hand-assembled program: an 8x8 diamond sprite at 0x200, a bouncing ball that moves 2 px per frame and reverses direction at the screen edges (bounds pre-checked so it never wraps), and pressing CHIP-8 key 5 (physical 'W') reverses both axes immediately. Add an HTML comment above the array explaining this.

=== CORRECTNESS NOTES ===
- The `0x5000` case must only match when the low nibble is 0 (SE Vx,Vy); the `0x5XY2/0x5XY3` SCHIP ops must be checked before it.
- The `0x8000` case must switch on `op & 0x000F`; `0x8XY6`/`0x8XYE` must honour the legacyShift checkbox.
- The `0xE000` case must switch on `op & 0x00FF` (0x9E / 0xA1).

- Never let `pc` exceed 0xFFF: mask with `& 0xFFF` on jumps and after increments.

- `0xFX07` LD Vx, DT: V[x] = delayTimer
